title: Scaling Training Data with Lossy Image Compression

problem.claim: Lossy compression can reduce image storage requirements but may degrade models trained on the compressed images, creating a storage–test-error trade-off.

gap.claim: Existing scaling laws address training data and parameter scaling for resource allocation, but the abstract identifies a need for a storage scaling law relating sample size and bits per image.

contributions.claim: The authors propose a storage scaling law describing the joint evolution of test error with sample size and bits per image.
The authors prove that the proposed law holds within a stylized model for image compression.
The authors use the law to optimize lossy compression levels and investigate randomizing the compression level.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report empirical verification of the storage scaling law on two computer vision tasks and extraction of the relevant parameters.
The authors report that, at a given storage budget, models trained on optimally compressed images have significantly smaller test error than models trained on the original data.

narrative_sequence.summary: Storage constraints motivate careful selection of image data formats and compression levels.
Lossy image compression reduces storage but can lower model quality, producing a trade-off between storage and test error.
The authors propose a storage scaling law for test error as a function of sample size and bits per image.
The law is proved in a stylized compression model and empirically evaluated on two computer vision tasks.
The law is applied to compression-level optimization, and the potential benefits of randomized compression levels are investigated.

source_observation.claim: The abstract reports that optimizing compression under a fixed storage budget yields lower test error than retaining the original data.

interpretation.claim: When storage is constrained, compression can be treated as a model-training design variable rather than only a preprocessing cost.

application.claim: Use a measured storage–performance relationship to jointly choose dataset size and per-example compression level.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this optimization transfers beyond the reported computer vision tasks or the stylized compression setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the two computer vision tasks.
The abstract does not provide the functional form or fitted parameters of the storage scaling law.
The abstract does not quantify the reported test-error improvements or storage budgets.
The abstract does not report the outcome of randomizing the compression level.
